noun:Arche.tx: From Middle High German arche, byform of more common arke, from Old High German arka, archa, from Proto-Germanic *arkō, from Latin arca. The expected German form is Arke. The ch-form is native in parts of Upper German. It was reinforced in the modern standard language by the Medieval Latin spelling archa.

adj:alternativ.tx: Borrowed from French alternatif, from Medieval Latin alternātīvus.

noun:Arschkarte.tx: Unknown, apparently from Arsch (“arse”) + Karte (“card”). According to a popular urban legend, the origin of this term can be found in soccer, more exactly the red card. Since on black-and-white televisions the yellow and red card could not be distinguished, the yellow card was held in the front pocket, while the referee pulled the red card from his trouser pocket. Since the 1990s.

noun:Altstadt.tx: From alt (“old”) + Stadt (“city”). Cognate with Low German Ooltstadt.

noun:Annexion.tx: Mid-19th century, from Latin annexio, semantically after English annexation.

noun:Ausflug.tx: Inherited from Middle High German uzvluc, uȥvluc. By surface analysis, deverbal from ausfliegen.

verb:anlassen.tx: From Middle High German anelāzen, from Old High German anelāzan. Equivalent to an- + lassen.

verb:austrinken.tx: From Middle High German ūȥtrinken. Equivalent to aus- + trinken.

adj:allerhand.tx: Univerbation of Middle High German aller hande.

noun:Abgott.tx: From Middle High German abgot, from Old High German abgot. By surface analysis, ab + Gott. Compare Dutch afgod.

noun:Aquifer.tx: From Latin aqua (“water”) + ferō (“to bring”). Compare English aquifer.

noun:Asymptote.tx: From Latin asymptōta, from the feminine of Ancient Greek ἀσύμπτωτος (asúmptōtos).

adj:antisemitisch.tx: First used in 1860 by Jewish scholar Moritz Steinschneider. See Wikipedia's article on the etymology and usage of the term

verb:absterben.tx: From Middle High German abestërben. Equivalent to ab- + sterben

verb:absteigen.tx: From Middle High German *abestīgen (attested in the noun abestīc, abesteic), derived from stīgen abe (verb + preposition). Analysable as ab- (“off, down”) + steigen (“to rise, mount”). Compare Dutch afstijgen, Gothic 𐌰𐍆𐍃𐍄𐌴𐌹𐌲𐌰𐌽 (afsteigan).

verb:aufsteigen.tx: From Middle High German ūfsteigen, ūfstīgen. Equivalent to auf- + steigen.

verb:aufschließen.tx: From Middle High German ūfslieȥen. Equivalent to auf- + schließen.

verb:auslaufen.tx: From Middle High German ūȥloufen. Equivalent to aus- + laufen. Cognate with Dutch uitlopen.

noun:Ambiente.tx: From Italian ambiente, from Latin ambiēns, present active participle of ambiō (“to surround”). Doublet of ambient.

noun:Alleskönner.tx: From alles (“all, everything”) + Könner (“expert, adept, master”), literally “all-can-doer”.

noun:Augenschein.tx: From Middle High German ougenschīn. By surface analysis, Auge + -n- + Schein.

noun:Abschlag.tx: From ab- + Schlag. Compare the noun Abschlagen, nominalisation of the verb abschlagen

noun:Advokat.tx: From Middle High German advocāte (14th c.), from Old French advocat, from Latin advocātus. Doublet of the earlier borrowing Vogt.

verb:anstrengen.tx: From Middle High German anestrengen. Equivalent to an- + streng + -en.

verb:aufregen.tx: From Middle High German ūfregen. Equivalent to auf- + regen.

noun:Argwohn.tx: From Middle High German arcwan, from Old High German argwan (“bad assumption, suspicion”); second element of compound is related to Wahn (“insanity”).

noun:Anstalt.tx: From Middle High German anstalt, deverbal from anstellen.

verb:aufleuchten.tx: From Middle High German ūfliuhten, equivalent to auf- + leuchten. Cognate with German Low German upluchten, uplüchten, Dutch oplichten, West Frisian opljochtsje, Saterland Frisian apljuchte, English uplight.

verb:ausheben.tx: From Middle High German ūȥheben, from Old High German ūȥheffen. Equivalent to aus- + heben.

noun:Aquarell.tx: Borrowed from Italian acquarella, older form of acquerello.

noun:Ausverkauf.tx: Deverbal from ausverkaufen. Equivalent to aus- + Verkauf. Compare Dutch uitverkoop.

verb:ausdenken.tx: aus- + denken. Cognate with English out + think ("think out").

noun:Achtel.tx: Inherited from Middle High German ahteteil n; compare achte + Teil.

verb:auferstehen.tx: From Middle High German ūferstān, from Old High German ūfirstantan, ūfirstān, ūfirstēn. Equivalent to auf- + erstehen.

noun:Azalee.tx: From New Latin azalea, from Ancient Greek ἀζαλέος (azaléos).

noun:Anfahrt.tx: From Middle High German anevart, from Old High German anafart. By surface analysis, deverbal from anfahren.

noun:Antidot.tx: From Latin antidotum, from Ancient Greek ἀντίδοτος (antídotos, “antidote, remedy”), from ἀντιδίδωμι (antidídōmi, “I give in return, repay”).

verb:anfallen.tx: From Middle High German anevallen, from Old High German anafallan, from Proto-West Germanic *anafallan. Equivalent to an- + fallen. Cognate with Dutch aanvallen.

verb:ansetzen.tx: Inherited from Middle High German anesetzen, from Old High German anasezzen. Analyzable as an- + setzen. Compare English onset.

verb:aufflammen.tx: From the compounding of the prefix auf- + flammen.

noun:Anrichte.tx: From Middle High German anrihte, from the verb anrihten (“to prepare”); see anrichten for more.

verb:anrichten.tx: From Middle High German anerichten, from Old High German anarihten. By surface analysis, an- + richten.

noun:Alaun.tx: Middle High German alūn, Old High German alūne, from Old French alun, from Latin alūmen.

verb:aussuchen.tx: From aus- + suchen. Compare English outseek.

noun:Alabaster.tx: From Middle High German alabaster, derived from Latin alabastrum, from Ancient Greek ἀλάβαστρος (alábastros), from earlier ἀλάβαστος (alábastos, “alabaster vase”). Cognate with Gothic 𐌰𐌻𐌰𐌱𐌰𐌻𐍃𐍄𐍂𐌰𐌿𐌽 (alabalstraun).

noun:Aikido.tx: Borrowed from Japanese 合気道 (あいきどう, aikidō), from Middle Chinese 合 (hop, “meet, unite”) + 氣 (kʰjɨ̀j, “spirit; breath”) + 道 (dáu, “way”).

verb:abrufen.tx: From Middle High German aberüefen. Equivalent to ab- + rufen. Cognate to Dutch afroepen.

verb:ablösen.tx: From Middle High German ablœsen, abelœsen, ablōsen, abelōsen, from Old High German abalōsen. Equivalent to ab- + lösen.

verb:ausrichten.tx: From Middle High German ūȥrihten. Equivalent to aus- + richten.

noun:Ausstieg.tx: Deverbal from aussteigen. By surface analysis, aus- + Stieg.

verb:abscheiden.tx: From Middle High German abescheiden, from Old High German abaskeidan, from Proto-West Germanic *abaskaiþan, from Proto-Germanic *abaskaiþaną. Equivalent to ab- + scheiden. Cognates include Dutch afscheiden, Old English ofscēadan and Gothic 𐌰𐍆𐍃𐌺𐌰𐌹𐌳𐌰𐌽 (afskaidan).

noun:Anilin.tx: From Portuguese anil (“indigo”) + -in (“-ine (organic compounds)”). Coined by German chemist Karl Julius Fritzsche in 1840.

noun:Atemnot.tx: From Atem + Not. Cognate with Luxembourgish Otemnout

noun:Alkali.tx: From French alcali, ultimately from Arabic اَلْقِلْي (al-qily, “alkali, ashes of the saltwort”).

noun:Ausscheidung.tx: aus- + Scheidung. Likely a calque of Latin excrētiō.

adj:abfällig.tx: From Middle High German abe-vellec, abevellec. By surface analysis, ab- + fällig. Also analyzable as Abfall + -ig.

adv:abfällig.tx: From Middle High German abe-vellec, abevellec. By surface analysis, ab- + fällig. Also analyzable as Abfall + -ig.

noun:Abnehmer.tx: abnehmen (“to buy”, as an extension of the basic “to take away” sense) + -er (agent noun suffix)

noun:Angesicht.tx: From Middle High German angesihte n (“viewing, visage, aspect”), alongside angesiht f, from Old High German anagisiht f (“viewing”). Compare Dutch aangezicht and further Swedish ansikte etc.

noun:Anthrazit.tx: From Latin anthracītis, from Ancient Greek ἀνθρακῖτις (anthrakîtis).

verb:ausfallen.tx: From Middle High German ūȥvallen. Equivalent to aus- + fallen.

verb:ausreden.tx: From Middle High German ūȥreden. Equivalent to aus- + reden.

verb:aufbereiten.tx: From Middle High German ūfbereiten. Equivalent to auf- + bereiten.

verb:anschwitzen.tx: an + schwitzen, because vegetables cooked in this way schwitzen (“sweat”) out their juices

verb:ausstatten.tx: From aus- + statten (“to stand up”). The core verb statten, now outdated in modern German, is from Middle High German staten (“to help do something; to add”).

verb:ätzen.tx: From Middle High German etzen, from Old High German ezzen, from Proto-West Germanic *attjan, from Proto-Germanic *atjaną. Etymologically, the causative verb to essen, with semantic narrowing.

verb:ausreichen.tx: From aus- + reichen. Compare English outreach, Dutch uitreiken.

adv:aneinander.tx: From Middle High German aneinander, aneeinander. Equivalent to an- + einander.

noun:Arbeitsbereich.tx: From Arbeit, the interfix -s-, and Bereich.

noun:Appaloosa.tx: Borrowed from English, possibly from Sahaptin. See appaloosa for more information.

verb:absagen.tx: From Middle High German abesagen. Equivalent to ab- + sagen. Cognate to Dutch afzeggen.

verb:ausstehen.tx: From Middle High German ūzstān, ūzstēn. Equivalent to aus- + stehen. Compare Dutch uitstaan.

noun:Arrest.tx: Borrowed from Medieval Latin arrestum, apparently a borrowing from Old French arest.

noun:Ami.tx: Clipping of Amerikaner + -i. Appears to have entered the German language during the Second World War and the following occupation era, hence probably first used in reference to American soldiers.

verb:aufwarten.tx: From Middle High German ūfwarten. Equivalent to auf- + warten.

noun:Anlauf.tx: From Middle High German anlouf, from Old High German anahlouf. Cognate with Luxembourgish Ulaf.

adv:allerorts.tx: From aller (“all”) + Ort (“place”) + -s (adverbial suffix) or all + -er- + -orts.

verb:abstellen.tx: From Middle High German abestellen. Equivalent to ab- + stellen.

noun:Andenken.tx: From Middle High German andenken, anedenken, equivalent to an- (“on”) + denken (“to think”). Compare Dutch aandenken.

verb:abtun.tx: From ab- (“off, away”) + tun (“to do”). Compare Dutch afdoen, English do off.

verb:angehören.tx: From Middle High German anegehœren. Equivalent to an- + gehören.

verb:absprechen.tx: From Middle High German abesprëchen (“to recant”). By surface analysis, ab- + sprechen.

verb:aufrichten.tx: From Middle High German ūfrihten, from Old High German ūfrihten. By surface analysis, auf- + richten.

intj:auweia.tx: Extended form of auwei, itself a variant of o weh. The diphthongisation may be expressive or may be from a regional variety such as Yiddish אוי וויי (oy vey).

verb:anführen.tx: From Middle High German anevüeren, from Old High German anafuoren. Equivalent to an- + führen.

noun:Angehöriger.tx: A substantivization (converting into a substantive) of the adjective angehörig (“belonging, affiliated”).

noun:Abrechnung.tx: From Late Middle High German aberechenunge. By surface analysis, abrechnen + -ung.

verb:ablegen.tx: ab- + legen. From Middle High German abelegen, from Old High German *abaleggen, from Proto-Germanic *abalagjaną.

verb:abrechnen.tx: From Middle High German aberëchenen. Analysable as ab- + rechnen. Compare Dutch afrekenen.

adj:amtlich.tx: From Middle High German ambetlich, from Old High German ambahtlīh. Equivalent to Amt (“office”) + -lich (“-ly”).

verb:aufbringen.tx: From Middle High German ūfbringen, equivalent to auf- + bringen. Cognate with German Low German upbrengen, Dutch opbrengen, English upbring.

verb:aufklären.tx: From auf- + klären, a calque of Middle Low German upklāren. Compare also Dutch opklaren.

verb:auslegen.tx: From Middle High German ūʒlegen (“to display, set out; interpret; pronounce; lend money”). By surface analysis, aus- + legen. Compare Yiddish אויסלייגן (oysleygn, “spell (a word); interpret; lend money”), Dutch uitleggen (“explain; interpret”), and rare English outlay (“to display; to spend/distribute money”).

verb:ausnehmen.tx: From Middle High German ūȥnëmen, from Old High German ūȥnëman, from Proto-West Germanic *ūtneman. Equivalent to aus- + nehmen.

verb:austragen.tx: From Middle High German ūztragen, from Old High German ūztragan, from Proto-West Germanic *ūtdragan. Equivalent to aus- + tragen.

verb:auswirken.tx: From Middle High German ūȥwürken. Equivalent to aus- + wirken.

noun:Anschein.tx: Related to an and Schein m. Cognate to Bavarian Aɑ(n)schei(n) (Egerländisch).

noun:Areal.tx: Borrowed from Medieval Latin āreāle, neuter of āreālis.

noun:Aufsehen.tx: From Middle High German ūfsehen n. By surface analysis, deverbal from aufsehen.

adj:ausladend.tx: From German Low German. Only secondarily adapted to the verb laden.

verb:anstehen.tx: From Middle High German anestān. Equivalent to an- + stehen.

verb:aufgreifen.tx: From Middle High German ūfgrīfen. Equivalent to auf- + greifen.

verb:anhaben.tx: From Middle High German anehaben, anhaben, from Old High German anahabēn, from Proto-West Germanic *anahabbjan, from Proto-Germanic *anahabjaną. Equivalent to an- + haben. Compare Dutch aanhebben, English have on, Gothic 𐌰𐌽𐌰𐌷𐌰𐌱𐌰𐌽 (anahaban).

noun:Auslese.tx: aus (“out of”) + Lese (“harvest”) (obviously cognate with lesen (“to read, select, pick”), which yields a high-quality connotation)

noun:Anstrich.tx: From Middle High German anstrich, synchronically analyzed as a nominal formation from anstreichen (“to paint, mark”).

verb:antun.tx: From Middle High German anetuon, from Old High German anatuon. Equivalent to an- + tun.

noun:Ausbund.tx: From ausbündig, from Middle Low German ūtbundich.

verb:aufsuchen.tx: From auf- + suchen. Compare English upseek.

noun:Aushilfe.tx: Deverbal from aushelfen. Analyzable as aus- + Hilfe.

verb:abblasen.tx: From Middle High German abblāsen, abeblāsen. Equivalent to ab- + blasen. Compare Dutch afblazen.

noun:Ausreise.tx: From the verb ausreisen (“to leave (the country)”).

verb:ausreisen.tx: From Middle High German ūzreisen. Equivalent to aus- + reisen.

adv:aufwärts.tx: From Middle High German *ūfwertes, *ūfwartes (attested only as ūfwart), from Old High German ūfwartes, equivalent to auf + -wärts.

verb:anspitzen.tx: From an- (“on”) + spitzen (“to point, make pointy”).

verb:abschwören.tx: From ab + schwören, calque of Latin abiuro

verb:ächzen.tx: From Middle High German echzen, achzen, echezen, achezen (“to say, groan, lament”), from Old High German *ahhizen, *ahhizzen (“to say ‘ah’”), attested in the verbal noun ahhizōt, derived from the interjection ah (“oh; ah; my; alas”), whence modern ach (idem).

noun:Antlitz.tx: From Middle High German antlitze, from Old High German antlizzi, from Proto-West Germanic *andawliti, from Proto-Germanic *andawlitją. Compare Swedish anlete.

noun:Allmacht.tx: Back-formation from allmächtig; compare also Dutch almacht. By surface analysis, all + Macht.

noun:Allotria.tx: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἀλλότρια (allótria, “strange or foreign things”), neuter plural substantive of ἀλλότριος (allótrios, “foreign, strange”), from ἄλλος (állos, “other”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂élyos (“other”).

verb:abkönnen.tx: Originally abhaben können, which is the same as haben können (“to be able to stand, endure”). The main verb haben was then felt as redundant and was ellipsed, as is common in colloquial German.

verb:aufdröseln.tx: With dialectal or hypercorrect d- from earlier (auf)tröseln, a German Low German and Central German word meaning “to turn; to untwist”. Compare Dutch treuzelen.

verb:abschrecken.tx: From Middle High German abeschrecken. Equivalent to ab- + schrecken.

noun:Apfelwein.tx: From Old High German apfulwīn, from Proto-West Germanic *appluwīn. Equivalent to Apfel + Wein.

verb:abschlagen.tx: From Middle High German abeslahen, from Old High German abaslahan. Equivalent to ab- + schlagen.

verb:abseilen.tx: From ab- + Seil + -en. First attested in the 17th century.

noun:Almanach.tx: First attested in the 16th century. Borrowed from Middle Dutch almanag (Flanders 1426), from Medieval Latin almanach (1267), from Andalusian Arabic مَنَاخ (manāḵ, “calendar”). The Ibero-Arabic term is of uncertain origin. See also almanaque. Perhaps originally derived from Medieval Greek ἀλμενιχιακά (almenikhiaká, “calendar”). The term is used by Eusebius while quoting from Porphyry's Epistle to …

noun:Akademiker.tx: Since the 18th century. Formed on the basis of or in analogy to the now obsolete synonyms Akademist and Akademikus.

noun:Alkoven.tx: From French alcôve f, from Spanish alcoba, from Arabic القبَة. The later final -n and masculine gender in German through association with unrelated Middle Low German koven (“stable, shed, nook”).

verb:abluchsen.tx: From ab- + luchsen. The latter from Low German lucksen, intensive form of luken, from Middle Low German lūken (“to pull, to pluck”), from Proto-Germanic *leukaną, which is related to Locke (“curl”, originally “tuft of hair”). In Standard German it was associated with an originally unrelated verb luchsen (“to peer, lurk”), which is derived from Luchs (“lynx”), an animal considered cunning and sharp-eyed.

noun:Abstecher.tx: From now-obsolete Dutch een afsteker maken (“to go by one of the boats of a ship”) (compare modern Dutch afsteken (“to set sail”)), synchronically analyzable as abstechen (“to cut out”) + -er; the German verb means in some contexts “to contrast, to diverge” and possibly also “to branch off” (compare Stichstraße (“small dead-end street branching off from a road”)), hence the further semantic development.

adj:anrüchig.tx: Borrowed from Middle Low German anrüchtig. See Gerücht for more.

verb:aufklaren.tx: Calque of Middle Low German upklāren.

verb:ausstaffieren.tx: Borrowed from Middle Low German ūtstafferen, equivalent to aus- + staffieren.

adv:allerorten.tx: Univerbation of the genitive of alle Orte m pl, from all (“all”) + Ort (“place”).

noun:Archivar.tx: From older Archivarius, from Latin archīvārius, from archīvum.

verb:auftragen.tx: From Middle High German ūftragen. By surface analysis, auf + tragen.

verb:abgehen.tx: From Middle High German abegān, from Old High German abagān. Equivalent to ab- + gehen.

noun:Ausstand.tx: From aus- + Stand. Cognate with English outstand.

adj:achtbar.tx: From Middle High German ahtbære, ahtebære. Equivalent to Acht + -bar. Potentially originally derived in part or in whole from Arabic أَكْبَر (ʔakbar, “big, great, powerful”) during the Crusades.

noun:Achtbarkeit.tx: From Middle High German ahtbærkeit. Equivalent to achtbar + -keit.

verb:aushelfen.tx: From Middle High German ūȥhëlfen. Equivalent to aus- + helfen. Compare English help out, Dutch uithelpen.

verb:aufsetzen.tx: From Middle High German ūfsetzen, from Old High German ūfsezzen. Equivalent to auf- + setzen.

verb:anlügen.tx: From Middle High German anliegen, aneliegen, from Old High German analiogan. Equivalent to an- + lügen.

verb:auftreiben.tx: From Middle High German ūftrīben, from Old High German ūftrīban. Equivalent to auf- + treiben.

noun:Assoziation.tx: From assoziieren on the model of French association, English association.

verb:auftun.tx: From Middle High German ūftuon. Equivalent to auf- + tun.

noun:Alpdruck.tx: Alp + Druck, because nightmares were formerly thought to be caused by an elf sitting on one's chest while one slept.

noun:Ahne.tx: From Middle High German ane, from Old High German ana (“grandmother”), from Proto-Germanic *anǭ, related to *anô (“ancestor”). Cognate with Swabian Ahna, Latin anus (“old woman, grandma”).

verb:aufführen.tx: Inherited from Middle High German ūfvüeren. By surface analysis, auf- + führen.

verb:anmaßen.tx: From Middle High German anemāzen. Equivalent to an- + Maß + -en.

verb:auserlesen.tx: From Middle High German ūzerlesen. Equivalent to aus- (“out”) + erlesen (“select, choose”).

verb:abkratzen.tx: From Middle High German abekratzen. Equivalent to ab- + kratzen. Compare Dutch opkrassen.

verb:abhacken.tx: From Middle High German abehacken. Equivalent to ab- + hacken.

noun:Ammer.tx: From Middle High German amer, from Old High German amaro, clipped from an assumed compound *amarofogal, from Old High German amar (“spelt, emmer”) for its preferred food. See Emmer.

noun:Ausraster.tx: From ausrasten (“to flip out, go berserk”) + -er.

adj:abendlich.tx: From Middle High German ābentlich, from Old High German ābandlīh, from Proto-West Germanic *ābanþlīk. Equivalent to Abend + -lich.

pt: to close or open a hinge
verb:aufklappen.tx: auf- (“up”) + klappen (“to close or open a hinge”)

adj:authentisch.tx: Borrowed from Ancient Greek αὐθεντικός (authentikós), with assimilation to native suffix -isch.

verb:ahnden.tx: From Middle High German anden, from Old High German antōn (“to get excited, be eager, be hotheaded, blame, avenge, punish”), from Proto-West Germanic *anadōn. Cognates include Old English andian (“to be envious”). The lengthening of the vowel is irregular; compare fahnden.

noun:Apfelbäckchen.tx: Apfel (“apple”) + Bäckchen, a diminutive form of Backe (“cheek”) + -chen. The word is documented since 1900. The cheeks are called that way because of their form and color similar to apples.

verb:austeilen.tx: From Middle High German ūzteilen. Equivalent to aus- + teilen.

verb:ansagen.tx: From Middle High German anesagen, from Old High German anasagēn, from Proto-West Germanic *anasaggjan. Equivalent to an- + sagen.

noun:Abendrot.tx: From Middle High German ābentrо̄t, from Old High German ābandrо̄to. Equivalent to Abend (“evening”) + Rot (“red color”).

verb:abbringen.tx: From Middle High German abebringen. Equivalent to ab- + bringen. Compare Dutch afbrengen.

noun:Antipathie.tx: From Latin antipathia, from Ancient Greek ἀντιπάθεια (antipátheia).

noun:Adaption.tx: From Medieval Latin adaptātiō, from Latin adaptare (“to adjust, fit”).

noun:Abc.tx: From Middle High German a. b. c., abecē; equivalent to A + B + C, the first three letters of the Latin and German alphabet.

verb:aufbleiben.tx: From Middle High German *ūfblīben, ūfbelīben (“to abide, to persist”). Equivalent to auf- + bleiben

noun:Anchovis.tx: Borrowed via Dutch ansjovis from Spanish anchovas, anchoas, plural of anchova, anchoa (“anchovy”), which is from Ligurian anciôa, through Vulgar Latin *apiuva from Latin aphyē, Ancient Greek ἀφύη (aphúē, “small fry”).

adj:abgebrüht.tx: Attested from the 16th century. Formally, ab (“off”) + gebrüht (“scalded, boiled”), based on the idea that things are hardened or “steeled” by boiling (e.g. eggs, compare hartgesotten, English hard-boiled). At the same time, perhaps originally, from vulgar Middle Low German brǖden (“to fuck”, also in the sense of “to afflict”), cognate and synonymous with early modern German bräuten, from Braut …

adj:ansässig.tx: From obsolete Ansasse (“local resident, neighbour”) + -ig, the former from an (“on, at”) + Sasse (“dweller, occupant”).

noun:Apokope.tx: Learned borrowing from Latin apocope, from Ancient Greek ἀποκοπή (apokopḗ).

verb:anzetteln.tx: Derived from Anzettel + -n. In weaving, the term Anzettel was used to describe the beginning of the process of stretching the yarn to form a woven fabric (then also known as a Zettel). This meaning of "beginning, starting something" was then extended. Synchronically analyzable as an- + zetteln.

noun:Antipode.tx: Late Latin, from Ancient Greek ἀντίποδες (antípodes), from ἀντί (antí, “against”) + πόδες (pódes), nominative plural of πούς (poús, “foot”).

noun:Augenmerk.tx: Loan translation and/or phonetic adaptation (17th c.) of Dutch oogmerk, from Middle Dutch ôghemerk. Analyzable as Auge + merken.

noun:Alk.tx: Borrowed from Swedish alka (used scientifically by Carl von Linné), from Old Norse alka, from Proto-Germanic *alkǭ.

noun:Agnosie.tx: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀγνωσία (agnōsía).

pron:alledem.tx: Univerbation of alle + dem, where alle is a now-obsolete alternative uninflected form of all.

noun:Aische.tx: Borrowed from Turkish Ayşe, from Arabic عَائِشَة (ʕāʔiša). The use as a common noun is due to the name's commonness among Turkish immigrants, possibly reinforced by the unrelated noun Ische (“gal, chick”).

noun:Amphitheater.tx: From Latin amphitheātrum. First attested in the 13th century.

noun:Ausguss.tx: From the verb ausgießen (“to pour out”).

verb:abschälen.tx: From Middle High German abescheln. Equivalent to ab- + schälen.

noun:Auslage.tx: Deverbal from auslegen, first attested around the mid 16th century. By surface analysis, aus- + Lage.

noun:Ablation.tx: Borrowed from Late Latin ablātiō (“a taking away”).

adj:abergläubig.tx: From Middle High German *abergeloubic, equivalent to Aberglaube + -ig. Cognate with Middle Low German āverlȫvich, āvergelȫvich (“superstitious”).

adj:abgefuckt.tx: Bilingual portmanteau of English fucked up and German abgewichst, a 1990s slang term of similar meaning.

adj:adipös.tx: From New Latin adipōsus, from Latin adeps (“fat, lard”).

adj:altbacken.tx: From Middle High German altbacken. By surface analysis, alt + gebacken with syncope of the prefix (as in hausbacken). Compare Dutch oudbakken.

adj:angeschickert.tx: Past participle of the less common verb anschickern, from schicker.

adj:apokryph.tx: From Latin apocryphus, from Ancient Greek ἀπόκρυφος (apókruphos).

adj:armselig.tx: In the 15th century derived from Middle High German armsal (“misery”). Compare also mühselig and trübselig

noun:Anziehsachen.tx: anziehen (“to put on”) + Sachen (“things”). First attested ca. 1900.

adj:atembar.tx: From atmen + -bar. The unpronounceable stem atm- takes a regular svarabhakti vowel; compare berechenbar etc.

adj:aufsässig.tx: Inherited from Middle High German ûfsetzec. By surface analysis, aufsitzen + -ig.

adj:axiomatisch.tx: From Ancient Greek ἀξιωμᾰτικός (axiōmătikós, “employing logical propositions”), equivalent to Axiom + -isch.

noun:Anger.tx: From Middle High German anger, from Old High German angar (“grass plot, arable or pasture land”), from Proto-Germanic *angraz. Cognate with Middle Dutch anger, Old Saxon angar, Old Norse angr (“meadow, pasture ground”).

noun:Anthologie.tx: From New Latin anthologia, since the mid 18th century.

noun:Arkade.tx: From French arcade (early 17th cent.), from Italian arcata

verb:anmuten.tx: From Middle High German anemuoten. Equivalent to an- + muten. Compare Middle Low German anmōden (“to ask for”).

noun:Anrede.tx: From an- + Rede or from anreden.

noun:Abwehrmechanismus.tx: Abwehr + Mechanismus, a concept in the Freudian model.

noun:Anhalt.tx: From Middle High German anhalt, anehalt (“stopping point, support, cause”), equivalent to an- + Halt.

phrase:aus die Maus.tx: A phrase used to end an episode of Die Sendung mit der Maus, a long-running children's TV programme in Germany.

noun:Abkunft.tx: From abkommen (“to derive from”). The second element's spelling is a continuation of Middle High German kunft, kumft, from Old High German chumft.

noun:Anorexie.tx: Derived from Ancient Greek ἀν- + ὄρεξις (an- + órexis)

noun:Akribie.tx: Borrowed from Ecclesiastical Latin acribia (18th c.), from Ancient Greek ᾰ̓κρῑ́βειᾰ (ăkrī́beiă), from ἀκριβής (akribḗs, “accurate, precise”). Compare Italian acribia.

noun:Armleuchter.tx: From Arm (“arm, upper limb”) + Leuchter (“candlestick”). The pejorative use is from the similarity with Arschloch (“arsehole”), or perhaps specifically the latter's plural form, Arschlöcher.

phrase:auf einem Bein kann man nicht ste.tx: Literally, “one cannot stand on one leg”. Compare Dutch op één been kun je niet staan.

noun:Attika.tx: Borrowed from Latin Attica, from Ancient Greek Ἀττική (Attikḗ)

noun:Action.tx: Unadapted borrowing from English action, from Latin āctiō. Doublet of Aktion and Aktie.

verb:abspannen.tx: From Middle High German abespannen. Equivalent to ab- + spannen.

noun:Ausbreitung.tx: From ausbreiten + -ung. Cognate with Luxembourgish Ausbreedung.

verb:anberaumen.tx: From Middle High German rāmen (“to make proposals, aim, strive”), Old High German rāmēn. Cognate with Old French aramir (“to define legally”), Old Saxon rāmōn (“to aim, strive”), Dutch beramen (“to fix”).

noun:Aufgang.tx: From Middle High German ūfganc, from Old High German ūfgang. Analyzable as deverbal from aufgehen.

verb:ausarbeiten.tx: From Middle High German ūȥarbeiten. Equivalent to aus- + arbeiten.

verb:auschecken.tx: Calque of English check out, equivalent to aus- + checken.

verb:anbellen.tx: From Middle High German anbëllen (see Middle High German bëllen). Equivalent to an- + bellen.

verb:aberkennen.tx: From Middle High German abeerkennen. Equivalent to ab- + erkennen.

verb:aufschneiden.tx: From Middle High German ūfsnīden, equivalent to auf- + schneiden. Compare Dutch opsnijden, German Low German upsnieden. The sense “to brag” apparently figuratively from “to cut food for serving” (so as to show one’s opulence).

verb:anbrennen.tx: From Middle High German anebrennen, anebrinnen, from Old High German anabrennen. Equivalent to an- + brennen.

verb:aufsitzen.tx: From Middle High German ūfsitzen. Equivalent to auf- + sitzen.

noun:Antiquitätenhändler.tx: From Antiquität (“antique”) + -en- (interfix or linking element) + Händler (“dealer, merchant”).

verb:abtörnen.tx: Partial calque of English turn off.

verb:antörnen.tx: Partial calque of English turn on.

verb:abdrücken.tx: From Middle High German abdrücken, abedrücken. Equivalent to ab- + drücken.

adv:auswärts.tx: From Middle High German ūzwertes, from Old High German ūzwertes. Analysable as aus + -wärts. Cognate with English outwards.

verb:abmachen.tx: From Middle High German abemachen. Equivalent to ab- + machen.

noun:Archetyp.tx: Borrowed from Latin archetypum, from Ancient Greek ἀρχέτυπον (arkhétupon, “model, pattern”).

verb:abwürgen.tx: From Middle High German abewürgen. Equivalent to ab- (“off”) + würgen (“to choke”).

verb:ausscheren.tx: 19th century, from nautical parlance, from Low German utscheren. By surface analysis, aus- (“out”) + scheren (“to escape”).

noun:Alsterwasser.tx: Alster + Wasser, after the tributary of the Elbe River.

verb:abstatten.tx: ab- + statten (“to bring into its stead”).

noun:Autokorso.tx: From Auto (“car”) + Korso (“celebratory row of vehicles”). The latter from Italian corso in the archaic sense of “horse race” (for which now corsa). In German, the word is chiefly used in compounds.

pt: to buckle up, fasten one's seat belt
noun:Anschnallgurt.tx: From anschnallen (“to buckle up, fasten one's seat belt”) + Gurt (“belt”).

verb:aushecken.tx: From Middle High German ūȥhecken. Equivalent to aus- + hecken.

verb:abrücken.tx: From Middle High German aberücken. Equivalent to ab- + rücken.

verb:aushungern.tx: From Middle High German ūȥhungern. Equivalent to aus- + hungern.

verb:anliegen.tx: From Middle High German aneligen, from Old High German analiggen. By surface analysis, an + liegen, literally “to lie on”. Compare Dutch aanliggen.

noun:Askari.tx: Borrowed from Swahili askari (“soldier”), from Arabic عَسْكَرِيّ (ʕaskariyy).

verb:antreffen.tx: From Middle High German anetrëffen, from Old High German anatrëffan. Equivalent to an- + treffen.

adv:allenthalben.tx: Inherited from Middle High German allenthalben.

verb:aufdrehen.tx: From Middle High German ūfdræjen. Equivalent to auf- + drehen. Compare English English upthrow, Dutch opdraaien.

verb:auflaufen.tx: From Middle High German ūfloufen. Equivalent to auf- + laufen. Cognate with Dutch oplopen.

noun:Abschuss.tx: Deverbal from abschießen. Compare Dutch afschot.

verb:anspeien.tx: From Middle High German anespīen, anespīwen, from Old High German anaspīwan. Equivalent to an- + speien.

verb:aufwerfen.tx: From Middle High German ūfwerfen, from Old High German ūfwerfan. Equivalent to auf- + werfen.

verb:abgewinnen.tx: From Middle High German abegewinnen. Equivalent to ab- + gewinnen.

verb:aussöhnen.tx: From Middle High German ūʒsüenen. Equivalent to aus- (“out-”) + a form of sühnen (“to atone”) with alternative vocalism, compare versöhnen.

verb:abhelfen.tx: From Middle High German abehëlfen. Equivalent to ab- + helfen.

verb:abschöpfen.tx: From Middle High German abeschepfen. Equivalent to ab- + schöpfen.

verb:auffassen.tx: From auf- (“up”) + fassen (“to seize, grasp”). Compare Dutch opvatten.

noun:Ansuchen.tx: From ansuchen (“to submit an application; to formally request”).

noun:Audi.tx: Borrowed from Latin audī (“listen!”), from audiō (“to listen”), translation of German Horch!, from Horch, after the founder August Horch.

verb:aufbahren.tx: From Middle High German ūfbāren. By surface analysis, auf- + Bahre + -en.

noun:Allel.tx: Clipping of Allelomorph, from English allelomorph.

verb:auswischen.tx: From Old High German ūȥwischen, from Middle High German ūȥwisken. Equivalent to aus- + wischen.

adv:allzeit.tx: From alle (“all”) + Zeit (“time”). Cognate with German Low German alltiet, Dutch altijd, Danish altid, Faroese altíð, Icelandic ætíð (only the second morpheme “tíð”), Norwegian Bokmål alltid, Norwegian Nynorsk alltid, Swedish alltid.

adv:allda.tx: From Middle High German aldā. Equivalent to all + da.

noun:Adobe.tx: Borrowed from English adobe, from Spanish adobe.

noun:Arglist.tx: From Middle High German arclist, from Old High German arglist. By surface analysis, arg (“bad”) + List (“cunning, craft”).

verb:auffahren.tx: From Middle High German ūfvaren, ūfvarn, from Old High German ūffaran, from Proto-West Germanic *uppfaran. Equivalent to auf- + fahren.

verb:austreiben.tx: From Middle High German ūztrīben, from Old High German ūztrīban. Equivalent to aus- + treiben.

noun:Autodafé.tx: Borrowed from Portuguese auto da fé.

verb:aufzwingen.tx: From Middle High German ūftwingen. Equivalent to auf- + zwingen.

verb:äffen.tx: From Middle High German effen. By surface analysis, Affe + -en.

verb:aufbieten.tx: From Middle High German ūfbieten. Equivalent to auf- + bieten.

verb:anklopfen.tx: From Middle High German anklopfen, aneklopfen, ane klophen. Equivalent to an- + klopfen

verb:abstehen.tx: From Middle High German abestēn, abestān. Equivalent to ab- + stehen.

verb:aufblasen.tx: From Middle High German ūfblāsen. Equivalent to auf- + blasen.

verb:ausfahren.tx: From Middle High German ūȥvaren, ūȥvarn, from Old High German ūȥfaran, from Proto-West Germanic *ūtfaran. Equivalent to aus- + fahren.

verb:anschießen.tx: From Middle High German aneschiezen, from Old High German anaskiozan. Equivalent to an- + schießen.

phrase:auch andere Mütter haben schöne T.tx: Literally, “other mothers also have beautiful daughters”.

verb:argwöhnen.tx: From an earlier argwohnen, from Middle High German arcwœnen, arcwænen, from Old High German argwānen.

noun:Adamskostüm.tx: From Adam (“Adam”) + Kostüm (“costume”). Compare the same in several languages.

verb:aufblähen.tx: From Middle High German ūfblæjen. Equivalent to auf + blähen.

noun:Ausguck.tx: aus- + Guck, nominalization of the verb gucken.

noun:Abstrich.tx: Deverbal from abstreichen. Cognate with Luxembourgish Ofstréch.

verb:ausbüxen.tx: Borrowed from Low German utbücksen. Possibly through Bangebüx (“scaredy pants”). By surface analysis, aus- + Buxe

noun:Adlatus.tx: Borrowed from Latin ad lătus (literally “on the side”).

noun:Abwurf.tx: Deverbal from abwerfen. By surface analysis, ab- + Wurf.

noun:Aberwitz.tx: From aber + Witz (“wit”). For aber- in privative function, compare Aberglaube; also compare Abgott (“false god, idol”).

noun:Ausfluss.tx: From Middle High German ūzvluz, from Old High German ūzfluz. By surface analysis, deverbal from ausfließen.

verb:ablecken.tx: From Middle High German abelecken. Equivalent to ab- + lecken.

noun:Austauschstudent.tx: From Austausch + Student or austauschen + Student.

noun:Austauschstudentin.tx: From Austauschstudent + -in or Austausch + Studentin or austauschen + Studentin.

noun:Altwarenhändler.tx: From Altware (“used good”) + -n- + Händler (“merchant, trader, dealer”).

noun:Affentheater.tx: From Affe + -n- + Theater (“to-do, fuss”, literally “monkey theater”).

noun:Abrasch.tx: Borrowed from Turkish abraş, from Ottoman Turkish ابراش, from Arabic أَبْرَش (ʔabraš, “dappled, mottled”).

adj:achtkantig.tx: From acht (“eight”) + Kante (“edge”) + -ig. The adverbial use is probably a pun on Low German Achterkant (“backside”, hence “buttocks”).

adv:achtkantig.tx: From acht (“eight”) + Kante (“edge”) + -ig. The adverbial use is probably a pun on Low German Achterkant (“backside”, hence “buttocks”).

verb:anstreichen.tx: From Middle High German anestrīchen. By surface analysis, an- + streichen.

adj:allererste.tx: From Early New High German allererst (adv.), from Middle High German allerērst, from Old High German allero ērist. By surface analysis, aller- (intensifying prefix) + erste (“first”)

noun:Account.tx: Unadapted borrowing from English account. The alternative pronunciations are due to the fact that German has no native initial /ə/ (though in the case of /ɛ-/ perhaps also to a falsely assumed English pronunciation).

noun:Ayahuasca.tx: Borrowed from Spanish ayahuasca, from Quechua ayawaska, from aya (“spirit, ancestor”) + waska (“vine”).

noun:Abschlussarbeit.tx: From Abschluss + Arbeit (“work”). The former word can be understood here as both “degree” and “completion, finish”.

verb:anmalen.tx: From Middle High German anemālen, from Old High German anamālen. Equivalent to an- + malen.

noun:Antiquariat.tx: Borrowed from New Latin antīquāriātus. By surface analysis, Antiquar + -at.

adj:anstandslos.tx: From Anstand (“objection; decency”) + -s- + -los (“-less”). The sense “objection” is chiefly obsolete except in the dated expression Anstand nehmen an (“to object to”). Still common is the derivative verb beanstanden.

verb:abrichten.tx: From Middle High German aberihten. Equivalent to ab- + richten. Cognate to Dutch africhten.

adj:angeheiratet.tx: From an- (“on, at, to”) + geheiratet (“married”), or past participle of a rare verb anheiraten.

verb:abnippeln.tx: From earlier abnibbeln, originally chiefly in Berlin. Further origin uncertain. Duden suggests ab- (“off”) + nibbeln (“to nibble”), perhaps from a sense of being nibbled away to nothing. Alternatively, possibly from Rotwelsch, by way of Yiddish, ultimately derived from Hebrew נבל (navál, “to wither, wilt”).

pt: to lose weight in an excessive way
noun:Abmagerung.tx: From abmagern (“to lose weight in an excessive way”) + -ung.

pt: to teem, to move in a confused crowd
verb:abwimmeln.tx: 19th century. Ostensibly from ab- (“off”) + wimmeln (“to teem, to move in a confused crowd”). The meaning could perhaps be understood as “to keep such a crowd away, move out of it”. However, a more satisfying interpretation as “to wave aside” can be based on cognate Low German wiëmeln, wemeln, which also has the sense “to wag, wave”. Compare German abwinken (“wave aside”), abwiegeln (“appease”), …

phrase:am Nasenring durch die Manege füh.tx: Literally, “to lead through the ring by the nose-ring”.

verb:aufblicken.tx: From Middle High German ūfblicken. By surface analysis, auf- + blicken.

noun:Agilität.tx: From French agilité (“agility”), from Latin agilitās (“activity, mobility, nimbleness, quickness, agility”).

phrase:außen hui, innen pfui.tx: Literally, “outside wow, inside yuck”. Perhaps inspired by Matthew 23:27, but the notion can also have arisen independently in everyday life.

verb:aufplustern.tx: 19th century, pleonastic compound from auf- + plustern (which latter already means the same thing).

phrase:Asche auf mein Haupt.tx: Literally, “ashes on my head”, from the Middle Eastern and thence Christian custom of sprinkling dust on one's head as a sign of penitence.

verb:anstechen.tx: From Middle High German anestechen, from Old High German anastehhan. Equivalent to an- + stechen.

verb:abgießen.tx: From Middle High German abegiezen. Equivalent to ab- + gießen.

noun:Aquaplaning.tx: Borrowed from English aquaplaning with a spelling pronunciation.

verb:ausbaldowern.tx: 19th century, from Rotwelsch (thieves’ cant). Equivalent to aus- + Baldower (“tipster, insider”) + -n. See the noun (which is now archaic) for more.

noun:Auslaufmodell.tx: From auslaufen (“to expire, be discontinued”) + Modell (“model”).

verb:äugen.tx: Formally from Middle High German öugen, ougen, from Old High German ougen, from Proto-West Germanic *augijan, all meaning “to show, let see”. By surface analysis, Auge (“eye”) + -en. The modern sense “to look” seems to be of northern origin, being first attested in Middle Low German ö̂gen, Middle Dutch ôgen (both 15th century). It only became common in standard German in the 19th century. There …

noun:Ausnüchterungszelle.tx: From Ausnüchterung + -s- + Zelle. Compare French cellule de dégrisement.

verb:abbusseln.tx: ab- + busseln. Compare Bavarian åbussln / obussln.

verb:abfaulen.tx: From Middle High German abe-vûlen, abevûlen, abvûlen. Equivalent to ab- + faulen.

noun:Arbeitsverweigerung.tx: From Arbeit (“work”) + -s- + Verweigerung (“to refuse, to deny”).

noun:Aushub.tx: Deverbal from ausheben (“to excavate, dig”). Also analyzable as aus- + Hub.

verb:abgraben.tx: From Middle High German abgraben, abegraben. Equivalent to ab- + graben. Cognate with Dutch afgraven.

verb:aushöhlen.tx: From Middle High German ūȥholn, from Old High German ūȥholо̄n. Equivalent to aus- + höhlen.

verb:auserwählen.tx: From Middle High German ūȥerweln. Equivalent to aus- + erwählen.

verb:auskaufen.tx: From Middle High German ūzkoufen. Equivalent to aus- + kaufen.

noun:Aufbahrung.tx: From Middle High German ūfbærunge. By surface analysis, Deverbal from aufbahren.

verb:aufsehen.tx: From Middle High German ūfsëhen, from Old High German ūfsëhan. By surface analysis, auf- + sehen.

verb:aufschwellen.tx: From Middle High German ūfswellen. Equivalent to auf- + schwellen.

verb:anraten.tx: From Middle High German anerāten, from Old High German anarātan. Equivalent to an- + raten.

verb:ausreiten.tx: From Middle High German ūzrīten, from Old High German ūzrītan, from Proto-West Germanic *ūtrīdan. Equivalent to aus- + reiten.

verb:anblasen.tx: From Middle High German aneblāsen, from Old High German anablāsan. Equivalent to an + blasen.

verb:aufbiegen.tx: From Middle High German ūfbiegen, from Old High German ūfbiogan. Equivalent to auf- + biegen.

verb:abschaben.tx: From Middle High German abeschaben, from Old High German abaskaban. Equivalent to ab- + schaben.

verb:ausschaben.tx: From Old High German ūzschaben. Equivalent to aus- + schaben.

verb:abwinken.tx: From ab- + winken, based on the wave of the hand as a gesture of refusal. Compare English wave off.

verb:ausknocken.tx: Partial calque of English knock out.

verb:anscheinen.tx: From Middle High German aneschīnen, from Old High German anaskīnan, from , from Proto-West Germanic *anaskīnan. Equivalent to an- + scheinen. Cognate with Dutch aanschijnen.

verb:auflecken.tx: From Middle High German ūflecken. Equivalent to auf- + lecken.

verb:anlecken.tx: From Middle High German anelecken. Equivalent to an- + lecken.

verb:abklopfen.tx: From Middle High German abeklopfen. Equivalent to ab- + klopfen.

verb:ausbringen.tx: By surface analysis, aus- (“out”) + bringen (“to bring”). Compare Dutch uitbrengen.

verb:anzahlen.tx: From Middle High German anzalen. Equivalent to an- + zahlen.

verb:abzahlen.tx: From Middle High German abezalen, abezaln. Equivalent to ab- + zahlen.

verb:anrennen.tx: From Middle High German anrennen, anerennen, from Old High German anarennen. Compare Dutch aanrennen.

verb:abgleiten.tx: From Middle High German abeglīten. Equivalent to ab- + gleiten.

verb:abzwacken.tx: From Middle High German abezwacken. Equivalent to ab- + zwacken.

verb:amnestieren.tx: Latin amnestia < Ancient Greek ἀμνηστία (amnēstía, “forgetfulness, pardon”)

noun:Autograph.tx: From Latin autographum, from Ancient Greek αὐτόγραφος (autógraphos). By surface analysis, auto- + -graph.

verb:aufmerken.tx: From late Middle High German ūfmerken. Equivalent to auf- + merken. Cognate with Dutch opmerken.

noun:Arbeitender.tx: From arbeitend; nominalization of the adjective arbeitend (“working”).

verb:aufmotzen.tx: From older aufmutzen (“to embellish”). Unrelated to motzen (“to grouch”).

noun:Apfelkorn.tx: From Apfel (“apple”) + Korn, short for Kornbrand (“kind of brandy”).

verb:angaffen.tx: Middle High German, by surface analysis, an- + gaffen.

verb:abschotten.tx: From ab- + Schott + -en, literally "to bulkhead off".
